title: County Breaks Ground on New Children's Crisis Residential Care Facility
description:
The County of San Diego broke ground today on a new Children’s Crisis Residential Care facility in Kearny Mesa that will be a first of its kind locally and fill a critical gap in the children’s system of care. 

The construction involves a full remodel of an existing 10,000‑square‑foot building and will be complete in late 2027. When the facility opens in early 2028, local youth experiencing a behavioral health crisis will have access to a welcoming and supportive 24/7 treatment center. 

The Behavioral Health Services Children’s Crisis Residential Care (CCRC) facility will operate as a short-term residential program. Once operational, the CCRC is expected to offer up to 16 beds and serve approximately 350 youth and families each year. 

As a regional resource, the CCRC will expand local capacity for children’s crisis care and support equitable access to essential behavioral health care by serving Medi-Cal eligible children and youth.  

Services will include timely mental health assessments, individualized treatment, stabilization and warm hand-offs to ongoing care. The purpose is to reduce unnecessary transfers and keep children connected to the support they need. 

The $12 million County infrastructure investment is funded largely through the Behavioral Health Continuum Infrastructure Program (BHCIP) along with other federal and state grants.
